title: Vinyl Plank Installation in Edmonds: 7 Questions to Ask Your Installer
meta: Seven questions to ask before booking vinyl plank installation in Edmonds: price, moisture, flatness, plank, trim, stairs, warranty. Wills Flooring answers.

blocks.lead: Ask any Edmonds vinyl plank installer seven questions before you book: what the labor rate includes, whether they moisture-test, how flat the floor must be and who levels it, which plank core and wear layer they recommend, how they handle baseboards and transitions, how stairs are done, and who stands behind the work.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring's answers are on our published price list: $2.50 per sq ft of labor, $100 per stair, 500 sq ft minimum, and a 1-year workmanship warranty. The plank itself, removal and any leveling are quoted at the free in-home estimate.

blocks.html: Vinyl plank is the floor most Edmonds homeowners choose when the 1960s carpet finally goes, whether in a Seaview rambler over a crawlspace, a Perrinville split-entry or a condo in the Bowl near the ferry. It is also the floor with the widest gap between a good installation and a bad one, because the product forgives nothing underneath it. These seven questions sort installers quickly. Ask them of everyone, including our vinyl plank installation crew.

blocks.note: Edmonds sits on the water and many older homes have crawlspaces with open vents. Moisture is the single most common cause of a vinyl plank floor that lifts or peaks in its first summer.

blocks.text: Question 3: How flat does my floor need to be, and who fixes it?

items.title: The number to ask for
items.text: Most rigid-core plank calls for a subfloor flat to within 3/16 in over 10 ft. Ask the installer what tolerance they work to. If they cannot name one, they are not checking.

items.title: What Edmonds ramblers show
items.text: 1950s to 70s houses in Seaview and Westgate often have joists that settled toward the center, humps where a wall was removed, and old vinyl layers of different thickness in the kitchen. All of it telegraphs through a click floor.

items.title: How it gets fixed
items.text: High spots are sanded or planed; low spots get a cement-based patch or self-leveling compound. Old sheet vinyl with a cushion backing usually has to come out. Each of these is a separate line on an honest quote.

items.title: Why it matters
items.text: Click joints flex over a dip and eventually crack or separate. Over a hump, the plank rocks and the joint opens. A hollow, clicking sound underfoot is the sign of a floor installed over an unflattened subfloor.

blocks.text: Questions 4 and 5: which plank, and what happens to the trim?

blocks.html: Question 4 is about the product. A good installer will recommend a rigid core (SPC or WPC) with a wear layer of at least 12 mil for bedrooms and 20 mil for kitchens, halls and homes with dogs, and will show you the sample in your own room. Be wary of anyone pushing one brand without saying why. Question 5 is about the edges of the room, and it has two honest answers.

a.title: Choose this when
items: You want the cleanest look with no quarter round
The baseboards are in good shape and come off without breaking
You are repainting anyway, since nail holes get filled and touched up
It is a whole-house job where the extra labor is worth it

b.tag: Leave baseboards, add quarter round or shoe
b.title: Choose this when
items: The trim is original to a 1950s Edmonds house and would splinter
You are not painting and do not want touch-ups
Budget matters more than the tiny reveal at the wall
The floor is going in a rental or a pre-sale refresh

blocks.text: Questions 6 and 7: stairs, and who stands behind the work

items.text: Stairs cannot float. Each tread is glued, the riser is faced with matching material, and a flush stair nose from the same collection finishes the edge. Ask to see a photo of the installer's stair work before booking.
items.note: Wills Flooring: $100 per stair. A Perrinville split-entry with 13 stairs and 700 sq ft: 700 × $2.50 + 13 × $100 = $3,050 labor

items.text: Ask for the contractor license number, proof of insurance and the written workmanship warranty. Ask whether the crew are employees and who you call if a plank lifts in August.
items.note: Wills Flooring: licensed and insured since 2013, 1-year workmanship warranty, one phone number, (425) 350-4435

items.text: An honest installer will tell you: manufacturing defects go to the plank maker, and moisture damage from a leak or crawlspace problem that arose after install is not workmanship. Settling this before the job avoids arguments after it.
items.note: Ask for both warranties, product and workmanship, in writing

blocks.text: Answers that should make you walk away

items.html: "Vinyl is waterproof, so we do not need to test anything." The plank is waterproof. The plywood, the adhesive and the click joints are not.
"We just go right over the old vinyl." Sometimes fine for a single well-bonded layer, but cushioned or multiple layers must come out, and old vinyl should be tested before it is disturbed.
"We can float the stairs." Floating plank on stairs comes loose. Treads must be glued and finished with a proper nose.
No expansion gap, or no answer about it. Rigid core still moves. A sunroom or south-facing Edmonds living room with no gap at the wall will peak in the first hot week.
A quote from the driveway. Nobody can quote flatness, moisture or removal without walking the rooms and opening a corner. Our moisture testing guide explains what a real check looks like.

blocks.title: The Edmonds crawlspace rule:
blocks.text: If your house is west of Highway 99 and built before 1980, assume the crawlspace matters. We check the vapor barrier and meter the subfloor at every estimate. A plywood reading over about 14 percent means the crawlspace gets fixed or dried before the plank goes down, not after.
Your seven-question checklist for the estimate

items.html: 1. What does the labor rate include, and what is the minimum?
2. Will you moisture-test the subfloor and look at the crawlspace, and write the readings down?
3. What flatness tolerance do you work to, and how will you fix my floor to meet it?
4. Which core and wear layer do you recommend for my rooms, and can I see it in my own light?
5. Baseboards off, or quarter round on, and what does each cost?
6. How exactly are the stairs done, and can I see photos?
7. License, insurance, and both warranties in writing?

faq.q: How much does vinyl plank installation cost in Edmonds?
faq.a: Wills Flooring charges $2.50 per sq ft of installation labor with a 500 sq ft minimum and $100 per stair. An 850 sq ft Seaview rambler is 850 × $2.50 = $2,125 in labor. The plank, underlayment, old-floor removal and any leveling are quoted separately at the free in-home estimate.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank need a moisture test if it is waterproof?
faq.a: Yes. The plank is waterproof, but the plywood or concrete under it is not, and moisture that rises from a damp crawlspace or slab will lift joints, grow mold under the floor and void product warranties. A good installer meters the subfloor and writes the reading on the quote.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank go over my old kitchen vinyl?
faq.a: Sometimes. One layer of well-bonded, non-cushioned sheet vinyl that is flat can be covered. Cushioned vinyl, multiple layers, or loose vinyl must come out. Vinyl from before the mid-1980s should be tested for asbestos before anyone disturbs it.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank be floated on stairs?
faq.a: No. Stair treads must be glued down and finished with a flush stair nose from the same collection, with the risers faced to match. Floating plank on stairs works loose and becomes a trip hazard. Wills Flooring charges $100 per stair for this work.

faq.q: What warranty should I expect on a vinyl plank installation?
faq.a: Two separate ones: a product warranty from the manufacturer covering wear and defects, and a workmanship warranty from the installer covering how it was put in. Wills Flooring provides a 1-year workmanship warranty and is licensed and insured. Ask for both in writing.
